Fixed `TopModule.sv` in place and verified it with an `iverilog` truth-table simulation.

- Changed `TopModule.sv:35` so `D` is generated from the four active-low decoder minterms for `001`, `010`, `100`, and `111`.
- Left `Co` unchanged at `TopModule.sv:36`; it already matched the full-subtractor borrow truth table.

SYMPTOM: `D` was always `0`, so the full subtractor produced the wrong difference for input combinations `001`, `010`, `100`, and `111`
ROOT CAUSE: `TopModule.sv:35` used `assign D = ~(Y1_n & Y2_n | Y4_n & Y7_n);`, which ORed two AND-groups of active-low decoder outputs; with one-hot active-low signals this expression collapses to `0` for every valid input instead of asserting on the selected minterms
FIX: replaced that line with `assign D = ~(Y1_n & Y2_n & Y4_n & Y7_n);` so `D` correctly goes high when any of the intended active-low minterms is selected
